methods: Computed from 199-sample native-resource-absorption timeseries in the original artifact. IACT is 1+2 sum of successive positive paired empirical autocorrelation coefficients, stopped at the first nonpositive pair, truncated before N/2. ESS=N/IACT is an approximation, not evidence of true stationarity. Early-late drift compares means of first and last 49 draws.
decision: The reported 199 chain samples are too autocorrelated (especially at 750/1500km, effective N only about 9-10 per chain) and the absorption outcome exhibits substantial first-to-last drift. Nominal p=0.005 values in the primary workflow must not be interpreted as valid independent permutation p-values. The observed-vs-null median contrasts are preliminary conditional descriptive results only. One finite extended-MCMC qualification is authorized in protocol SPATIAL_NULL_EXTENDED_MIXING_GATE_20261015.md; if it fails, stop rather than retune.
limits: The ESS estimate is an autocorrelation heuristic and may overstate effective information for nonstationary chains.
Geographical models condition on coarse polygon representative points and source-specific host records.
No evidence of butterfly competition, colonization, or local larval fitness.
